title: Dynamic Short Convolutions Improve Transformers
abstract: arXiv:2606.03825v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Transformers have become the dominant architecture for large language models, largely due to the scalability and flexibility of attention, feed-forward layers, residual connections, and normalization. This paper introduces dynamic short convolutions as an additional neural network primitive for improving Transformers. Unlike static short convolutions, dynamic convolutions use input-dependent filters, which preserves the locality bias of convolution while increasing expressivity. Motivating experiments show that applying dynamic short convolutions to key, query, and value representations improves performance on challenging associative recall tasks compared with static convolutional variants. Across language-modeling experiments ranging from 150M to 2B parameters, dynamic convolutions consistently outperform standard Transformers and Transformers augmented with static short convolutions. translated_abstract: Transformer已成为大型语言模型的主导架构，这主要归功于注意力机制、前馈层、残差连接和归一化所带来的可扩展性与灵活性。本文引入动态短卷积作为一种额外的神经网络原语，用于改进Transformer。与静态短卷积不同，动态卷积使用依赖于输入的滤波器，在增强表达能力的同时保留了卷积的局部性偏置。启发性实验表明，将动态短卷积应用于键、查询和值表示，与静态卷积变体相比，能够在具有挑战性的联想回忆任务上取得更好的性能。在从1.5亿（150M）到20亿（2B）参数规模的语言建模实验中，动态卷积始终优于标准Transformer以及通过静态短卷积增强的Transformer。拟合缩放定律的结果表明可获得1.33倍的……
tldr: 本文提出动态短卷积作为一种新的神经网络原语，利用依赖输入的滤波器在保留卷积局部性偏置的同时提升表达能力，在150M至2B参数的语言建模实验中持续优于标准Transformer及静态短卷积增强版本。
en_tdlr: Dynamic short convolutions use input-dependent filters to preserve convolution's locality bias while increasing expressivity, consistently outperforming standard Transformers across language-modeling experiments from 150M to 2B parameters.
